title: Rapidus 2nm pilot line
summary: Japan's state-backed attempt to return to leading-edge logic manufacturing.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Rapidus, backed by Japanese industry and government, opened a pilot line in Chitose, Hokkaido, in 2025 with a target of 2nm mass production in 2027. It works with IBM and imec on process technology and aims at low-volume, high-value customers such as edge AI and custom silicon rather than smartphone volume. The venture's success depends on yield learning at a speed no new entrant has achieved in decades.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Pilot
Estimated window 2025–2027
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

A successful Rapidus would change supply-chain geography for advanced logic; a failed one would be a very expensive lesson in yield curves.

What Would Change The View

  • Pilot-line yield and customer commitments.
  • Funding beyond the first production target.
  • Tool and materials ecosystem readiness.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
